recent_articles.title: KARD, Khandre condemn assault on BRIMS resident doctor - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Karnataka Association of Resident Doctors (KARD)** and **Bidar district in-charge Minister Eshwar B. Khandre** condemned the alleged assault of a resident doctor at **Bidar Institute of Medical Sciences (BRIMS)**, urging the state government to improve security for doctors working in public hospitals.  A letter sent to the Director of Medical Education on Friday stated that **Tukaram**, a 28-year-old orthopaedic resident doctor, was allegedly assaulted while attending to an injured patient in the casualty ward around 1 a.m. on Friday.

recent_articles.title: Mumbai, Maharashtra emerging as key hubs for global investment and clean energy partnerships, say diplomats - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Consul Generals** from **Australia** and **Finland** highlighted the growing investment opportunities in Mumbai and Maharashtra, emphasizing infrastructure development, clean energy, education, and technology sectors.  They praised Mumbai's transformation, citing projects like the Coastal Road and metro expansion as drivers of investor confidence. Both diplomats acknowledged challenges faced by foreign investors, including regulatory clarity and streamlined approval systems. Despite these challenges, they expressed optimism about Mumbai's long-term trajectory as a global economic hub.

recent_articles.title: KERC directs Escoms to give consumers 15 clear days to pay bills - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Karnataka Electricity Regulatory Commission (KERC)** has mandated that all electricity distribution companies provide consumers with a minimum of 15 days to pay their bills from the actual bill issuance date, not the scheduled billing date. The order, effective June 1st, requires all bills to clearly state the generation date and time, and mandates payment due dates be calculated accordingly.  The commission emphasized that late or extended billing cycles do not exempt Escoms from providing consumers with sufficient payment time.

recent_articles.title: Bowring Hospital wall collapse: Lokayukta probe finds major safety lapses - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A **Lokayukta** inquiry into the fatal wall collapse at the **Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital** in Shivajinagar, Karnataka, has revealed multiple structural and administrative failures. The investigation found that the wall was constructed beyond permissible height limits, had been damaged previously, and lacked proper drainage systems and retaining walls.  The inquiry also highlighted negligence by authorities who failed to monitor dangerous structures and encroachments. **Senior IAS and IPS officers**, officials from various departments, and hospital authorities appeared before the **Lokayukta** for questioning. The **Lokayukta** directed authorities to identify similar unsafe structures and take preventive measures.

recent_articles.title: Deepa Jewellers, Cotec Healthcare receive Sebi approval for IPOs - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Deepa Jewellers**, a Hyderabad-based company specializing in hallmarked gold jewelry processing and trading, plans to raise funds through an IPO consisting of a fresh issue and offer-for-sale. The IPO will include up to Rs 250 crore worth of shares from the company and up to 1.18 crore shares offered for sale by promoters **Ashish Agarwal** and **Seema Agarwal**.  **Cotec Healthcare**, a contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) serving pharmaceutical companies, also received Sebi approval for its IPO. The company manufactures formulations across various therapeutic segments and operates a manufacturing facility in Roorkee with an installed capacity of over 4 billion units.

recent_articles.title: Will TVK government take ‘firm stand’ on Mekedatu project, asks Palaniswami - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Edappadi K. Palaniswami**, general secretary of the **AIADMK**, questioned the **Tamil Nadu** government's ability to protect its interests in the **Mekedatu balancing reservoir project** on the Cauvery river, citing the reported support of the **Congress** party and concerns about potential power-sharing agreements.  **D.K. Shivakumar**, Karnataka’s Deputy Chief Minister, reportedly stated that Tamil Nadu had no right to object to the project, while **T.T.V. Dhinakaran**, founder of the **AMMK**, echoed these concerns.

recent_articles.title: States should be allowed to conduct CET for medical courses: CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Siddaramaiah** called for the decentralization of the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) and urged **States** to have the opportunity to conduct their own Common Entrance Tests (CET) for medical courses. He argued that education is a concurrent list subject, allowing states to independently administer entrance exams for professional courses within the federal system.

recent_articles.title: Fake call centres duping U.S. citizens busted in Bengaluru, man from Delhi, another from U.P. arrested - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Karnataka State Cyber Command** officials raided four fake call centers in Bengaluru, uncovering a sophisticated operation that defrauded U.S. citizens by impersonating a prominent American accounting firm. The accused, Prashanth and Akash, allegedly collected millions of rupees from victims through fake tax advice, license renewal services, and counterfeit software keys.  The investigation revealed the use of shell companies to launder money and a network of over 120 employees trained to deceive victims using US accents. **Pronab Mohanty**, Director General of Cyber Command, stated that further investigations will focus on tracing the money trail and identifying bank accounts used in the fraud.

recent_articles.title: Congress workers clash with police in Jaipur during stir against NEET-UG paper leak - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** party workers clashed with **police** in **Rajasthan** on Thursday during a protest against the NEET-UG exam paper leak.  Led by **State Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra**, the protesters demanded the resignation of **Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan** and the dissolution of the **National Testing Agency**. The demonstrators, carrying banners and placards, were forcibly dispersed using water cannons. Some protesters suffered minor injuries.

recent_articles.title: Suo motu case against top Karnataka officials after raids expose illegal sand mining in Bagalkot - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lokayukta Police** in **Karnataka** have registered a suo motu case against several senior government officials, including the Director of the Mines and Geology Department in Bengaluru and the Bagalkot Deputy Commissioner, for alleged large-scale illegal sand mining in the Krishna river bed. The investigation followed complaints about rampant illegal mining activities in Bagalkot district and revealed indiscriminate excavation using heavy machinery in violation of environmental norms.  The **Lokayukta Police** conducted raids across Bagalkot district on May 21, seizing equipment and uncovering large quantities of illegally extracted sand.  Further investigations are underway to determine the extent of the illegal activity and hold those responsible accountable.

recent_articles.title: Mega merger incoming: Should you buy PFC, REC shares ahead of merger? Here's what analysts say - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nirmala Sitharaman**, the **Union Finance Minister**, announced plans to restructure **Power Finance Corporation (PFC)** and **Rural Electrification Corporation (REC)** for streamlined operations. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved a proposal where PFC acquired 52.63% of the government's holding in REC, consolidating them into a single balance sheet.  Analysts suggest investors consider staggered exposure to PFC and REC as the merger process is subject to regulatory approvals and structural adjustments. While PFC offers better visibility due to its parent status, REC presents a merger-arbitrage opportunity with higher event risk depending on the swap ratio.

recent_articles.title: Stray dog euthanasia: Bengaluru examining legally permissible options for ‘rabid, ill, or aggressive dogs’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bengaluru’s corporations** are grappling with the Supreme Court's ruling that allows for euthanasia of "rabid, incurably ill or demonstrably dangerous" dogs. The court emphasized qualified veterinary assessments and adherence to existing animal welfare laws.  However, a lack of clear guidelines on aggression levels has raised concerns about potential misuse by civic officials. Animal rights activist Arun Prasad warns this could lead to unnecessary dog killings. Meanwhile, Nevina Kamath, a co-petitioner in a previous case regarding stray dog euthanasia, plans to file a review petition against the new ruling.

recent_articles.title: PM busy handing out candies in Italy amid economic storm at home, says Congress - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** president Mallikarjun Kharge and **Rahul Gandhi** criticized the **Narendra Modi** government's economic policies, accusing it of prioritizing publicity over addressing rising inflation, unemployment, and weakening economic indicators.  **Kharge** highlighted the increase in average debt per Indian and wealth concentration among billionaires, while **Gandhi** criticized the Prime Minister's focus on foreign trips during a time of economic distress. Congress officials also pointed to the rupee's decline, falling foreign exchange reserves, and large investor outflows as evidence of government mismanagement.

recent_articles.title: Bidadi township: Deve Gowda announces stir against project; DKS hits back - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **H.D. Deve Gowda**, former Prime Minister, launched a campaign against the proposed Bidadi township project, claiming it targets fertile agricultural land and is driven by a "land business." He accused the **Siddaramaiah** government of facilitating this project under the guise of urban development, drawing parallels with previous satellite township projects that were withdrawn due to public opposition. **D.K. Shivakumar**, Deputy Chief Minister, countered Gowda's accusations, alleging that the Kumaraswamy family amassed wealth through real estate dealings and initiated similar projects in the past.

recent_articles.title: NEET paper leak row: Congress demands resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leaders demanded the resignation of **Dharmendra Pradhan**, the **Union Education Minister**, over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal.  They accused the government of a "money-making racket" involving people linked to the ruling establishment and claimed that the incident had caused immense trauma for 22 lakh students. **Rahul Gandhi** called for the Prime Minister's intervention, while **Mallikarjun Kharge**, the Congress president, alleged that the Modi government was undermining student credibility through repeated paper leaks.  **Jairam Ramesh**, a Congress general secretary, criticized the government's lack of action and incompetence in addressing exam reforms.

recent_articles.title: Medical Education Minister demands court-monitored probe into NEET paper leak - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Karnataka Medical Education Minister Sharan Prakash Patil** criticized the ongoing investigation into the NEET question paper leak, calling for a court-monitored probe. He expressed concerns that the **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)**'s current investigation lacked transparency and confidence, suggesting powerful individuals were involved in orchestrating the scandal to manipulate MBBS seat sales.

recent_articles.title: BJP protests State government’s decision to withdraw uniform rule in educational institutions - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **BJP** district unit members protested against the **State government's** decision to withdraw uniform regulations in educational institutions, arguing that it would disrupt discipline and academic atmosphere. The protesters, including former MP Umesh Jadhav and BJP leaders Baburao Chavan, Sudha Halkai, Chandrakant Patil, and Ashok Bagli, demanded intervention from the Governor to retain the policy. They claimed uniforms promote secular values and reduce socioeconomic disparities among students.

recent_articles.title: Submerged temple emerges as Bhavanisagar Dam level drops - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Bhavanisagar Dam**'s water level dropping to 59 ft. has revealed the dilapidated **Sri Madhava Perumal Temple**, which was submerged during construction in the 1940s and 1950s.  A study of inscriptions on the temple premises found it to be located at the confluence of the Bhavani and Moyar rivers, once a significant trade route connecting Kongu with Karnataka and Kerala. The site is believed to have been ruled by the Hoysalas and served as the location for a fort built by **Madhava Perumal Dhandanayaka**, a general appointed by King Veera Ballala III.  The temple was last visible in 2024 when the water level dropped, and fishermen report that portions of the structure become visible again at lower water levels.

recent_articles.title: Insensitivity and lack of concern, alleges Congress on Center’s silence over U.P. storm deaths - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following a powerful storm that killed at least 111 people in Uttar Pradesh, the **Uttar Pradesh** government directed Ministers to assess the situation and provide financial assistance. The **Congress** party criticized the **Union Government's** lack of response, highlighting the condolences from Russian President Vladimir Putin as evidence of their insensitivity.  The **Uttar Pradesh** Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced a ₹4 lakh compensation for families who lost loved ones and directed officials to ensure relief for farmers and livestock owners.

recent_articles.title: Monsoon to reach Kerala on May 26, says IMD - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** predicts the southwest monsoon will advance into Kerala on May 26, a day earlier than its usual June 1 arrival.  While this year's monsoon onset is anticipated to be early, there are concerns about below-normal rainfall. The IMD has historically been accurate in predicting the monsoon's arrival over Kerala, with only one exception in 2015. **M. Ravichandran**, Secretary of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, stated that after the monsoon onset, a period of heavy rain is expected for the next five days.  The IMD has warned of potential drought impacts due to reduced rainfall and the ongoing El Nino phenomenon.

recent_articles.title: Joyride horse dies of highly contagious zoonotic disease disease in Chennai; Tamil Nadu goes into alert mode - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The ICAR–National Research Centre on Equines (NRCE)** confirmed that a horse used for joyrides in the city has died from glanders, a highly contagious bacterial disease affecting equines. **The Besant Memorial Animal Dispensary (BMAD)** alerted authorities after noticing the horse's weakened condition and sent samples to the NRCE for testing. The NRCE advised the Tamil Nadu Animal Husbandry Department to isolate and monitor all equines in the area, implement surveillance and testing protocols, and regulate inter-state movement of horses. **The Tamil Nadu Animal Welfare Board** has requested that samples be collected from all joyride horses.

recent_articles.title: Supreme Court closes plea of Goa Congress leader after his death from snakebite - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** closed the plea of deceased **Ketan Bhatikar**, a Congress candidate for the Ponda Assembly seat, challenging a Bombay High Court order cancelling the bypoll.  Bhatikar died from a snakebite on Thursday and his lawyer requested the court to leave the larger question of law open while closing the proceedings. The High Court had earlier canceled the bypoll citing violation of the Representation of the People Act as less than one year remained in the term of the Assembly.

recent_articles.title: Sebi approves IPO plans of Neolite Lightings, Aspri Spirits and SS Retail - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Neolite ZKW Lightings**, a manufacturer of automotive lighting products, plans to raise Rs 600 crore through a combination of fresh issue and offer-for-sale. The IPO will be used for setting up a greenfield manufacturing facility in Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu, expanding existing operations, and repaying borrowings. **Neolite ZKW Lightings** has a significant market share in India's commercial vehicle lighting segment and serves over 40 OEM customers. Meanwhile, **Aspri Spirits**, an importer and distributor of international wine and spirits, received Sebi approval for its public issue with a proposed IPO of up to Rs 140 crore.  SS Retail, another company seeking regulatory clearance, plans to raise Rs 500 crore through its IPO, which will be used for expansion and growth.

recent_articles.title: Supreme Court allows actor Darshan to revive bail plea in a year if no ‘substantial progress’ in trial - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** expressed disappointment over the slow pace of the trial in the 2024 Renukaswamy murder case involving Kannada actor Darshan Thoogudeepa. The court granted him liberty to renew his bail plea if there is no "substantial progress" within a year, directing the trial court to ensure regular witness examinations and avoid adjournments on flimsy grounds.  The top court also directed prison authorities to provide Mr. Darshan with basic amenities as per jail manual rules and for the Karnataka High Court to address the issue of the vacant presiding officer position at the trial court.

recent_articles.title: Get Cauvery water released by Karnataka: Farmers - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Coordination Committee of All Farmers Associations of Tamil Nadu** urged the **Tamil Nadu government** to prioritize releasing the state's water share from the Cauvery river, citing a need for immediate action given last season's kuruvai cultivation. The committee also expressed concern over an agreement between **the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation (TNCSC)** and the National Consumer Cooperative Federation (NCCF) for paddy procurement, urging the government to ensure timely payment of sales proceeds to farmers.

recent_articles.title: ‘Limited’ religious symbols to be allowed with uniforms in Karnataka schools and colleges - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Karnataka government** withdrew its 2022 order requiring prescribed uniforms in educational institutions and replaced it with a new order allowing students to wear “limited” traditional and faith-based symbols alongside their uniforms.  Minister for School Education and Literacy **Madhu Bangarappa** stated that the decision aims to promote secular values and equal respect for all religions and traditions within schools, while maintaining institutional discipline.

recent_articles.title: Women’s coalition urges speedy implementation of 33% reservation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Members of the National Coalition for Women’s Reservation-Karnataka** have called on the government to immediately implement the women's reservation Act, arguing that linking it to future Census and delimitation exercises is delaying progress. They criticized the delay in delivering equal political representation for women, who constitute 50% of the population, and questioned the need to link implementation with these processes.  The coalition has been advocating for the Act's implementation since 1996 and has intensified nationwide mobilization efforts to achieve this goal.

recent_articles.title: Lawrence Bishnoi gang stakes claim on gunfire outside Diljit Dosanjh's manager in Karnal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema** alleged that the **Lawrence Bishnoi gang** was responsible for an alleged firing incident outside the residence of Diljit Dosanjh's manager in Haryana.  **Tyson Bishnoi, Arzoo Bishnoi, and Hari Boxer**, purportedly acting on behalf of the **Bishnoi gang**, claimed responsibility for the incident via social media. **Cheema** accused the **BJP** of using gangsters to intimidate Punjabis who refuse to join their party. The **Haryana Police** have not received a complaint from the manager or his family and found no evidence at the scene.

recent_articles.title: Congress unveils ‘Bhu Guarantee’ in Karnataka - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the **Deputy Chief Minister** of Karnataka, unveiled the "sixth guarantee" — Bhu Guarantee — which includes a 60% discount on conversion fees for B-Khata to A-Khata properties within Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) limits. The scheme also offers a 50% reduction in regularisation costs for buildings constructed before 2008 on BDA land, and a 15% setback relaxation as per the Town Planning Act. These announcements come amidst discussions about holding civic elections in Bengaluru this year.  The government aims to encourage property conversions and regularizations, but faces challenges with low application rates due to high fees previously associated with these processes.

recent_articles.title: Karnataka SC/ST employees’ association objects to new roster - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Karnataka State Government** announced a 400-point roster for the recruitment of 56,432 posts. The **Karnataka State Government Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes Employees’ Association** objected to the first 50 points being unscientific and argued it would negatively impact SC community candidates in Group ‘A’ and Group ‘B’ posts.  The association urged five Dalit Ministers to review and create a new, scientific roster.

recent_articles.title: SC asks Centre to consider States’ pleas for funds for CCTVs in police stations - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** urged the **Union government** to fully implement the Assistance to States and Union Territories for Modernisation of Police (ASUMP) scheme, which provides funds for installing CCTV cameras in police stations and a centralized monitoring dashboard. The court expressed concerns over non-functional CCTV cameras in Udaipur police stations and directed the Centre to consider requests from states for funding.  The ASUMP scheme has been extended until September 30, 2026, with most states initiating steps towards compliance. However, Jharkhand was criticized for not installing any CCTV cameras, despite receiving funds under the scheme. The court also cautioned against releasing funds without due diligence to prevent misappropriation.

recent_articles.title: What you need to know about Karnataka’s Rohith Vemula Bill - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Karnataka** government has approved the revised **Rohith Vemula** Bill, 2026. The bill aims to prevent discrimination and injustice for students, faculty, and staff from scheduled castes and tribes (SC/ST) by guaranteeing equal access to education in all higher educational institutions across the state.

recent_articles.title: Cong MLCs meet Surjewala, seeks clarity on leadership issue - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **MLCs** from the **Congress** government in Karnataka met with **Randeep Singh Surjewala**, a **Congress** general secretary, in New Delhi to discuss potential leadership changes. The MLCs requested an early clarification on the issue and also demanded that at least five members be included in the state cabinet if there is a reshuffle.

recent_articles.title: ST delegation meets CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Siddaramaiah**, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, has promised to convene an all-party meeting to discuss the inclusion of a 56% reservation matrix in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution.  He also assured **V.S. Ugrappa**, former MP and leader of the Samana Manaskara Vedike, that he will take an all-party delegation to **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** to advocate for this legislation. The state government has been working to overturn a legal stay on the 56% reservation, with legal experts being consulted and a special leave petition potentially filed in the Supreme Court.

recent_articles.title: AICC begins consultations with Kerala leaders in New Delhi to decide on Congress’ CM candidate - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, **Sonia Gandhi**, and **Mallikarjun Kharge** met with top Kerala leaders in New Delhi on Tuesday to discuss the selection of a Chief Minister nominee for the state. The high command is seeking bipartisan support from former KPCC presidents, Congress MLAs-elect, and other key figures to restore organizational stability after the party's recent victory.  The meeting considered several potential candidates, including **K.C. Venugopal**, **V.D. Satheesan**, **Ramesh Chennithala**, and **Priyanka Gandhi Vadra**.  **K. Muraleedharan**, a KPCC insider, stated that the high command would consider popular opinion in addition to legislative party numbers when making their decision.

recent_articles.title: The challenge to not breach the limit - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Karnataka government** announced the resumption of public recruitment for 56,432 posts after a year-long hiatus due to reservation issues. The new quota matrix has been met with resentment from job aspirants and some groups, as it altered the overall reservation percentage and internal quotas for Scheduled Castes (SCs).

recent_articles.title: Election results 2026: Why welfare policies aren't winning polls in India like it used to
recent_articles.rephrased_article: India's welfare politics, once a key electoral tool, is facing challenges. While cash transfers and subsidized services have become the norm across parties, recent state elections suggest that extensive welfare delivery alone is no longer enough to secure incumbency.  **Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress**, for example, lost power in West Bengal despite its women-centric welfare schemes. **The Bharatiya Janata Party** has capitalized on expanding welfare architecture, including women's self-help groups and administrative efficiency, while voters are increasingly demanding more than just welfare benefits.  Political scientists argue that this shift signifies a move from the floor of Indian politics to the ceiling, where parties must build coalitions around broader issues like job creation and economic mobility.

recent_articles.title: Two persons arrested for burglary in Tirupattur - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **G. Nagaraj**, 60, and **B. Vaishnavi**, 26, were arrested in Tirupattur for stealing gold jewelry, silver objects, and cash from the home of a retired government school teacher. The theft occurred on April 9th after the couple returned from Chennai.  **Shymala Devi**, Superintendent of Police, formed special teams to investigate the case, which included analyzing CCTV footage and tracing mobile phone signals. The suspects were apprehended in KGF Colony and are currently held at the sub-jail in Tirupattur.

recent_articles.title: LPG price surge pushes auto, taxi operators to seek subsidy for shift to CNG, EV - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Federation of Private Transport Associations** has urged the **State** and **Union governments** to provide financial assistance for auto and taxi operators to transition to CNG and electric vehicles. The federation cites rising LPG prices and supply concerns as reasons for their request, noting that drivers are willing to switch but face high conversion costs without government support.  The association has formally submitted representations to both the State Transport Department and the Union government seeking subsidies to ease the process.

recent_articles.title: Workers under CITU Karnataka demand revocation of Labour Codes, burn copies of the Act - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Workers** across **Karnataka**, under the **Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU)**, protested against newly-implemented central labor codes. Protests involved burning copies of the codes and taking out processions, with demonstrations occurring at workplaces and district centers. The **CITU Karnataka State Committee** called for a state-wide protest on May 12, 2026, urging the government to not implement the codes in the state due to concerns about worker rights.

recent_articles.title: World Deadliest Snakes: King Cobra Capitals: 10 countries where the world’s deadliest snake thrives | World News - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **King cobras**, the world's longest venomous snake, inhabit forests and wetlands across South and Southeast Asia.  Top countries with significant populations include India, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Nepal, Vietnam, Cambodia, and China. These countries support diverse king cobra habitats, which are threatened by habitat loss, deforestation, and poaching.  Conservation efforts focus on protecting forest corridors and educating communities about safe coexistence with these fascinating creatures.
